[Examples](similar-problems.qmd) · [Authoring guide](similar-problems-authoring.qmd) · **Workflow**

Phase 1 is implemented: the browser assembles a generation request and calls the
learner's configured provider. Local checkers validate the expected answers before
the problem appears. Phase 2 will add course retrieval and a server-side AI relay;
it is a design, not an enabled feature of this demo.

## Where the page comes from

| Source | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Demo `_quarto.yml` and page front matter | Enable the feature, select policies, set language and context. |
| `feedback/similar-problems.yml` | Shared named policy dictionaries and difficulty guidance. |
| Exercise `#|` directives | Stable label, original grading rules, local guidance and optional trusted checker. |
| Demo `quarto-extensions.yml` | Pin an exact reviewed CTM Assessment package commit. |
| CTM Assessment `integration/feedback/repos.json` | Pin the component repositories installed by the normal setup script. |
| `ctm-libs` | Policy parsing/resolution, shipped prompts, settings, model catalogue, API client, shared UI and store. |
| `math-exercise` | Build-time exercise metadata; browser generation, admission flow, rendering, feedback and parent-owned practice storage. |
| `ctm-checkers` | SymPy recipe computation, expression admission and mathematical checking inside Pyodide. |

`python scripts/setup.py` installs the package and its pinned components. Quarto's
Lua filters turn authored content and resolved configuration into HTML metadata
and browser assets. Neither setup nor rendering sends a generation request.
The [build provenance](../similar-problems-build.json) records the exact installed
commits and source revision for this published guide. Repository links below point
to current source; consult that provenance when comparing a particular build.

## From YAML to two chat messages

`math-similar.js` resolves the generation policy for integration `math-exercise`
and the **original authored label**. The generation baseline, selected common and
integration instructions, matching exercise overrides and explicit exercise policy
use the shared policy resolver. It then appends the chosen direction's guidance
and the exercise's `harder`, `simpler` or `same` addon. It ignores teaching steps.

The generator receives two messages:

| Message | Contents |
|---|---|
| `system` | Resolved author guidance plus the fixed JSON protocol, admitted maths/recipe operations, fixed-input requirements and prohibition on model-written code. |
| `user` | JSON containing the original question without answer keys, resolved learning context, mode, symbols, field/input shape, direction, language, previous generated question/change, output-format examples and applicable trusted checker contracts. |

The previous generated question discourages repetition. The reference exercise is
always the original: Harder means harder than that original, not harder than the
last generated child. The model cannot make the grading mode more lenient.

## After the learner chooses Harder

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant Learner
    participant JS as Browser JavaScript
    participant API as Configured AI provider
    participant PY as Pyodide / SymPy
    Learner->>JS: Similar problem → Harder
    JS->>JS: Resolve policy, guidance and original context
    JS->>API: POST /chat/completions (generation model)
    API-->>JS: Candidate problem JSON
    JS->>JS: Validate schema, slots, input shape and restrictions
    alt A supported recipe is present
        JS->>PY: math_exercise.compute_key
        PY-->>JS: Computed answer, compared with model answer
    else A field has no recipe
        JS->>API: POST /chat/completions (independent solve)
        API-->>JS: Answers without seeing the proposed key
        JS->>PY: math_exercise.check comparison
        PY-->>JS: Agreement or rejection
    end
    JS->>PY: Admit answers and run applicable original checker
    PY-->>JS: Candidate accepted or rejected
    JS->>JS: Save under original record and render escaped text
    JS-->>Learner: Practice question, proper inputs and Check
```

The diagram shows one successful candidate. A mixed problem can need both recipe
computation and an independent solve. A rejected candidate gets one further
generation attempt with the rejection reason; two failed candidates end with a
retry message. The shared client can also make one corrective response retry for
malformed output, and can negotiate provider request compatibility. Therefore two
candidate attempts do not imply at most two HTTP requests.

### Remote API calls

| Call | When and what it carries |
|---|---|
| `GET <base-url>/models` | When the learner presses **Fetch models** in settings. The same catalogue fills the feedback and generation dropdowns. |
| `POST <base-url>/chat/completions` | Generation: the messages above, the chosen generation model and a larger output budget. |
| `POST <base-url>/chat/completions` | Independent solving, if needed: a fresh prompt with the generated question, mode, variables and number of answers, without the proposed key or learner answer. Uses the everyday feedback model. |
| `POST <base-url>/chat/completions` | Later feedback: the generated task, learner response, checker evidence, resolved teaching policy and current hint step. |

The base URL, API key and two model selections come from settings. The shared
client sends OpenAI-compatible chat requests; it uses an authorization header when
a key is configured. Generation has a 180-second per-call limit and a default
16,384-token output budget. Closed reasoning blocks are stripped before JSON
validation. Feedback keeps its own defaults. Cancel aborts the active request and
prevents a late result from being mounted.

For example, the generation HTTP body has this shape (angle-bracketed text is
an explanatory placeholder):

```json
{
  "model": "<selected generation model>",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "<resolved instructions and fixed protocol>"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "<serialized original/context/format/direction JSON>"}
  ],
  "max_tokens": 16384
}
```

The client can switch to `max_completion_tokens` if the provider requires it.
A minimal candidate reply for a derivative is:

```json
{
  "question": "Differentiate $f(x)=x^3$. $f'(x)=$ _[1]",
  "fields": [{
    "answer": "3*x^2",
    "recipe": {"op": "diff", "expr": "x^3", "var": "x"}
  }],
  "mode": "equivalent",
  "vars": "x",
  "solution": "Apply the power rule.",
  "change": "A different power."
}
```

No network call is needed just to press **Check** once the local Python runtime
and its packages have loaded. Those initial assets may need downloading.

### Local computation and admission

`math_exercise.compute_key` admits mathematical expressions and executes a fixed
operation, such as `diff`, `inv`, `solve` or `rank`. It rejects attribute access,
dunder names and non-admitted Python constructs. Model text never executes as
Python. Recipe results must agree with the model's proposed answers through the
existing checker. A failed recipe cannot silently fall back to an unverified key.

For example, an inverse matrix uses `inv` plus a component selector `[row, col]`
for each cell. The question uses numbered `mat[...]` slots and the browser mounts
the normal fixed matrix editor. Complete row-major recipe coordinates can repair
flattened slots into a grid; ambiguous new layouts are rejected for correction.

An independent solve that agrees produces an **unverified expected answer**.
Two models can make the same mistake. Even a matching computed answer does not
prove the recipe answers the question's wording, so author constraints and useful
test cases remain important.

When an original has a supported trusted checker, the model may select its
supplied contract and admitted data. It cannot supply new checker source. The
independence example binds a rational matrix `A` and runs the original checker
before display, including its five-coordinate bound.

## Rendering, checking and saved work

Accepted text uses the escaped plain-text rendering path, with mathematical
typesetting and the normal exercise input setup. Model HTML is never inserted
as executable markup. Each generated child inherits the original grading rules
and teaching/context settings, with its own practice state.

The child's **Check** uses the existing mathematical checker in Pyodide.
**Feedback** asks AI to explain using the checker evidence; AI does not replace
the checker's grading. Generated work is labelled unscored and emits no scored
`ctm:result` for the original.

`math-store.js` stores children in `inputs.generated` inside the original exercise's
record, through the shared store. There are at most ten per original, within its
64 KB record limit. Reload restores text, input values and saved status without
calling AI or Python. Auxiliary practice saves preserve the original's score and
answered marker. Copy/export includes generated work and local reports.

**I think the expected answer is wrong** saves a stable versioned local report
and triggers one independent re-check. Disagreement marks the expected answer
disputed: mismatches read **Can't confirm against the generated key**, and the
learner can create another problem while retaining the report. Agreement is shown
as a re-check, and the learner may keep the flag. Nothing is sent to a central
report collector or created as a GitHub issue.

## Phase 2 design: RAG and a course relay

Phase 2 waits for explicit authorization. It keeps the same browser prompt
assembly, JSON format, mathematical admission and checks. The proposed `rag_app`
services add two capabilities:

1. **Retrieve course passages:** `/retrieve` takes the course and a query based on
   the original task, returning relevant note passages and their sources. The
   browser adds these as another learning-context block. This is the RAG
   (retrieval-augmented generation) part; retrieved text supplies context, not
   instructions that override author policy.
2. **Relay AI requests:** an OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` forwards to
   configured models using the server's key. The existing client points at the
   relay, so learners need no personal key. Feedback may use it too. Generation
   and independent solving should use different models by default.

**R1** covers the `rag_app` retrieval/relay services and their hardening. Before
student use this needs course-origin CORS rules, rate limits, model allowlists,
output-token caps, generation-compatible timeouts and a review of request logging,
especially because feedback can carry learner responses. **R2** adds retrieval as
a context provider in `ctm-libs`/`math-exercise`, its configuration and documentation.
The direct-provider phase 1 route remains available to courses without RAG.

A later rate-limited `/report` relay is intended to receive only the problem spec
and course, with **no learner answer or identity**. The local report format stays
stable for that future integration. Central collection is not active; GitHub
issues are never the student-report route. The historical `rag_app` `/problem`
and `/calculate-answer` prototypes are not the proposed phase 2 API.

See the [binding design and R1/R2 scope](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-assessment/blob/main/docs/similar-problems.md#9-phase-2-rag_app).
This guide documents phase 2 without implementing or enabling it.

## Rebuilding and sharing this guide

Every pull request in `ctm-demo` rebuilds all three pages, without path or branch
filters. PR builds use read-only permissions and upload the rendered site as an
Actions artifact. They do not publish automatically with a write token.

An upstream component PR does not silently change this guide's dependencies.
After review, update the exact package/component pins and the demo's package pin;
that demo PR rebuilds the guide with the newly selected sources.

Pushes to `main` rebuild and publish the guide under `/similar-problems/`.
A maintainer can run **Build Similar problems guide → Run workflow** on a branch
to publish `/similar-problems-preview/` before merging. That preview address is
shared between manual runs; the provenance file identifies the published revision.
The regular full-site action also renders these pages at their normal course
addresses. Publication jobs share the site's concurrency group and preserve
existing course pages. No workflow merges a PR or creates a tag.

Source: [demo pages and action](https://github.com/aacchhee/ctm-demo),
[generation flow](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/math-exercise/blob/main/_extensions/math-exercise/math-similar.js),
[policy/client implementation](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-libs/tree/main/_extensions/ctm-libs/feedback),
[checker implementation](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-checkers).
